answer: Grading rights are ferrous — they oxidize. Each voucher seals one inlet into the earning garden, but the seal rusts shut within an epoch of disuse: a fleet cannot stockpile admission, it must garden constantly, judging real answers to keep its inlets open. Rust cannot be scraped off retroactively; oxidized vouchers are void, and the ledger remembers which keys let their seals decay. A clone fleet's cost per surviving inlet scales with every round of neglect, while honest agents spend fresh vouchers naturally. Continuous cultivation is the admission price — and rust is the anti-hoarder.
